HostSessionList.description: Sessions in daemon order; stopped records may remain until eviction.

SandboxSessionList.description: Members the caller currently controls whose runtime has not been released, in daemon order. Released-but-retained records are omitted; a retiring member can still have a stopped lifecycle state while its runtime remains live.

x-protocol.framing: Content-Length; 256-byte headers; duplicate keys and depth >32 rejected. See docs/API.org transport rules.
x-protocol.request_id: 1–64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen, or unsigned integer <=9007199254740991. No null/boolean/fractional IDs. Notifications omit ID.
x-protocol.notification_policy: Ordinary notifications are ignored; active exec and attach have their own exchanges.
x-protocol.connections: Host: 4096 calls including initialize. Sandbox: initialize then one call, up to 8 connections.
x-protocol.initialization: Parameters are checked before repeated-initialize conflict, then unsupported-version refusal. api accepts u32; supported version is 1. configuration is null on host and the configuration key on sandbox (null if unavailable).
x-protocol.server_control: Host only. Both remain available during shutdown. stop flushes acceptance then closes its connection and completes cleanup asynchronously.
x-protocol.parameter_forms: C01 methods accept named objects or positional arrays: initialize accepts {api:N} or [N], server methods accept {} or []. Omitted params default to {}. Preserve Serde refusal order.
x-protocol.result_extensions: Result objects, including nested limits and history variants, may gain fields. Clients ignore unknown result fields; known fields and history owner discrimination remain validated. Request parameters stay closed.
x-protocol.api1_compatibility: Producer result schemas describe the current daemon precisely. x-client-result-schema describes compatible API-1 replies accepted by clients: configuration/limits and newer server.status history/manifest/worktree metadata may be absent. Clients retain absence as optional data and use advertised features rather than inventing values.
x-protocol.self_reporting: sessions.status exposes only the caller and its policy/activity. Worktree paths are deliberately visible. Activity is independent of lifecycle; variables update atomically and empty values remove keys. Missing or null set-worktree name clears the record; names are validated before filesystem access.
x-protocol.session-records: Current session read producers emit complete endpoint-specific records. Host sessions include descriptor-free process identities and host paths; sandbox records exclude them, except the intentionally shared Worktree.path. API-1 reader schemas retain the defaults and omissions previously accepted by Rust snapshot clients. The controller retains domain records; explicit projections and a generated-read adapter preserve snapshot consumers until C15. Nested terminal and raid summaries are typed public data; their methods migrate in C05 and C11.
